extracted.intended_audience: scholars and students of humor/cultural studies; comedians and critics interested in political/rebellious humor
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria for judging 'rebellious' or resistant jokes in American culture — whether they connect to current anxieties, serve social processing, and who they resonate with. Useful for scholars analyzing joke cycles and for practitioners assessing topical/cultural effectiveness of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addresses a current cultural anxiety
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the joke address a current cultural anxiety?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topical currency is essential: funny jokes plug into current anxieties; stale topics don't land. The 'barometer reading' must match the moment for the joke to be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processes collective fear or shock
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joke cycles often emerge around traumatic events (e.g., Challenger, 9/11) and function to process collective shock. Effective jokes help make sense of trauma; unsuccessful attempts at processing may fail to land or feel inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lands with a particular in-group (group identification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it land with a particular in-group?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience must recognize their own anxieties in the joke — in-group humor lands harder. Evaluate whether the target audience will perceive the shared frame of reference and feel included rather than alienated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punches up at power
rubrics_metrics.description: Does it punch up at power?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebellious humor is a form of resistance and is especially consequential when it targets those in power (political repression, elites). Assess whether the joke challenges authority or merely reinforces status quos; 'punching up' is a hallmark of effective rebellious humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provides catharsis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes about scary or traumatic subjects can allow audiences to release fear. Successful cathartic jokes produce relief; failed catharsis results in uncomfortable silence. Consider emotional release as an evaluative dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmissibility / ease of spread
rubrics_metrics.description: Easy transmission gives the joke tremendous impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because jokes circulate in everyday language before reaching formal performers, assess whether a joke's form/content is easily shareable and memetic. High transmissibility amplifies social effect and speeds uptake across communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and lifecycle (joke-cycle dynamics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Joke cycles emerge around traumatic events, process collective shock, then fade as the shock resolves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate a joke's place in a broader cycle: is it appropriately timed (not premature, not stale)? Consider whether the joke contributes to the arc of a joke cycle — emergence, spread, saturation, and decline — as part of its cultural function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source diversity and perspective
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor comes from many sources: whites, Blacks, women, Hispanics, conservatives and liberals, public workers and students, the powerless and power brokers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing rebellious humor, note the identity and social position of the joke-teller; diverse origins affect interpretation and legitimacy. The same joke may be received differently depending on whether it comes from an in-group, an out-group, or an authority figure.
